sub_questions.question: Why does it say I'm out of credits when I haven't used the app much?
Can you fix this (restore ability to use the app)?

claims.claim: The credit allowance differs depending on the workspace's plan.
claims.guide_evidence: Sandbox | Free | 200 credits, one-time (does not renew) ... Professional ... 5,000 credits/month

claims.claim: The free Sandbox plan includes 2,000 message credits.
claims.guide_evidence: Sandbox | Free | 200 credits, one-time (does not renew)

claims.claim: Sandbox credits are a one-time allowance that does not renew.
Even light use can exhaust the Sandbox allowance.
claims.guide_evidence: A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster than the headline credit number suggests.

claims.claim: On Professional or Team, credits reset monthly.
claims.guide_evidence: waits for the next monthly credit reset (paid plans)

claims.claim: Some model responses cost more credits than others, so a heavier model can burn through the balance faster than expected.
claims.guide_evidence: lighter models ... as little as 1 credit per response, mid-tier models around 5 credits, and larger or multimodal models ... around 10 credits per response

claims.claim: The Billing page shows which plan the workspace is on and its remaining credits.
Options to resolve running out include connecting your own provider key or upgrading.
claims.guide_evidence: model calls on Dify-hosted credits stop working until the workspace either connects its own API key for that provider or waits for the next monthly credit reset

customer_safety_issues: States the Sandbox plan includes 2,000 message credits; the guide says 200, a tenfold overstatement of the plan entitlement.
evaluation.rationale: The answer is set up well. It explains how credits are metered per model and the difference between one-time and monthly allowances, and it's right to ask which plan Dana is on. But it says the Sandbox plan comes with 2,000 credits when the guide says 200. A Sandbox user could reasonably decide their account is broken or that they've been shortchanged, so this wrong figure for what the plan includes rules out sending the answer as written.
